jobs.description:
TITLE: Program Manager

FLSA CLASSIFICATION: Non-Exempt

HOURS: Full-Time

RESPONSIBLE TO: City Director – Los Angeles

DIRECT REPORTS: Casa Milagrosa Staff

LOCATION: 161. S. Alvarado St. Los Angeles, CA 90057

SALARY: $25.00 per hour, paid bi-weekly

Mission

Depaul USA supports homeless and marginalized people, providing people experiencing homelessness with purpose and hope for a positive future. Our vision is that everyone has a place to call home and a stake in his or her community. In cities across the nation, we meet people where they are to address their needs. Through a combination of homelessness services and a growing social enterprise portfolio, Depaul USA is innovating and bringing real solutions to those facing homelessness.

Depaul USA Is a Growing, National, Not-for-profit Organization That Serves More Than 7,000 People Annually And Has a Combined Operating And Capital Budget In Excess Of $12.5 Million. Our Vincentian Values Underpin What We Do

We celebrate the potential of people;
We put our words into action;
We aim to take a wider role in civil society; and
We believe in rights and responsibilities.

Please visit www.depaulusa.org to learn more.

Depaul USA is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace, and we are firmly committed to creating an equitable and inclusive environment for all employees. If you need a reasonable accommodation in any part of the hiring process, please let us know.

Position Description

The Program Manager (PM) is responsible for the overall management and daily operations of Casa Milagrosa, a day resource center serving individuals experiencing homelessness or housing instability. The PM oversees all center staff, volunteers, facility operations, and program services to ensure a safe, welcoming, and effective environment for participants. The PM reports to the Los Angeles City Director, who provides overall oversight of Casa Milagrosa.

Primary Duties And Responsibilities

Essential Job Functions

Oversees the overall daily operations of Casa Milagrosa, ensuring the center operates effectively and meets the needs of participants.
Manages daily opening and closing procedures, staffing coverage, and coordination of program activities.
Maintains a safe, clean, organized, and welcoming environment for participants, staff, volunteers, and visitors.
Oversees facility needs, maintenance coordination, and the ordering, purchasing, and inventory of food, beverages, snacks, cleaning products, program supplies, and other materials necessary for daily operations.
Ensures program procedures, safety expectations, and organizational policies are consistently followed.
Responds to emergencies, participant concerns, conflicts, and other urgent situations.
Directly supervises all staff assigned to Casa Milagrosa and coordinates volunteer activities.
Provides regular individual supervision, guidance, training, and feedback to support staff performance and professional development.
Coordinates staff schedules, responsibilities, and daily activities to ensure appropriate coverage and effective service delivery.
Addresses staff performance and accountability concerns and communicates significant staffing or operational issues to the Los Angeles City Director.
Ensures participants are treated with dignity and respect and receive appropriate support in a safe and welcoming environment.
Works closely with the Case Manager to ensure participant needs are addressed and appropriate services and resources are available.
Provides direct assistance to participants as needed, including helping them access housing, employment opportunities, community resources, and other supportive services.
Assists with participant intake, enrollment, and referrals while the Case Manager maintains primary responsibility for assigned client caseloads and case management services.
Addresses participant concerns and difficult situations in a sensitive, professional, and appropriate manner.
Maintains program records and tracks participant enrollment, attendance, activities, outputs, and outcomes.
Ensures required program documentation, reports, and statistics are completed accurately and submitted within established timelines.
Monitors program activities and identifies opportunities to improve service delivery and overall program effectiveness.
Works with the Los Angeles City Director to review program needs, performance, and operational priorities.

Additional Tasks and Responsibilities

Builds and maintains positive working relationships with community organizations, housing providers, service agencies, and other community stakeholders.
Participates in community coalition meetings and other collaborative activities that support the program's mission.
Assists with facility tours and provides information about Casa Milagrosa to visitors, volunteers, community partners, and other stakeholders.
Collaborates with the Case Manager, Los Angeles City Director, and other organizational staff to support program goals and organizational priorities.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

General Responsibilities

Stays informed of current local and national events, trends, and issues that impact Depaul USA’s work with people experiencing homelessness.
Strives continuously to develop the role in collaboration with the supervisor to ensure that all tasks are undertaken effectively and appropriately, meeting the strategic goals and objectives of Depaul USA.
Participates in internal and external meetings as required, attends training events, conferences, and other functions as necessary.
Participates in regular supervision and annual evaluations, identifying personal developmental and training needs.
Ensures adherence to all Depaul USA policies and procedures, particularly those relating to Health and Safety, Safeguarding, and the Code of Practice and Confidentiality.
Contributes to the effective implementation of Depaul USA’s Equal Opportunities Policy as it affects both the organization and its work with this participant group.
Undertakes the role in a professional manner, maintaining a highquality standard of work in accordance with the Vision, Mission, and Values of Depaul USA.
Undertakes any other duties that may be required which are commensurate with the role.

Qualifications

Qualifications

The ideal Program Manager will have experience managing programs and working with individuals experiencing homelessness or housing instability, including those facing mental health challenges, cognitive disabilities, and substance use disorders. The candidate should have an understanding of community resources and social service systems, along with the leadership and organizational skills necessary to oversee daily program operations and supervise staff. The successful candidate will possess the following qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Social Work or a closely related field, with at least two years of experience working with individuals experiencing homelessness and/or behavioral health challenges.
Experience supervising staff, coordinating program activities, or managing daily operations in a social services or nonprofit setting preferred.
Strong communication, interpersonal, problemsolving, and conflict resolution skills.
Ability to organize and prioritize multiple responsibilities, coordinate people and activities, and delegate effectively.
Sound judgment, decisionmaking skills, and the ability to work independently while knowing when to seek guidance.
Strong computer skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
Spanish fluency strongly preferred.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions. In the course of performing the job, the person in this position typically spends time sitting, standing, climbing stairs, walking, driving, carrying (20lbs), lifting (20lbs), operating a computer keyboard, and making and receiving telephone calls. Subjected to outside environmental conditions.

Work Schedule:

Primarily inperson at Casa Milagrosa in Los Angeles, CA.
Regular schedule is Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. 3:30 p.m. Pacific Time.
Must be available to support special events and program activities that may take place during evenings and weekends.

Benefits:

Medical, dental, and vision coverage options for the employee and eligible dependents.
Company provided Basic Life/AD&D & Short/Long Term disability policies.
401(k) Retirement plan with employer match.
Generous Vacation, Sick, and Personal leave and 10 Observed holidays.

Background Checks:

A background check (including a criminal records check) must be completed as part of the hiring process. Failure to satisfactorily complete the background check may affect application status or applicants’ employment status.

It is not intended to be and should not be construed as an all-inclusive list of all the responsibilities, skills, or working conditions associated with the position. Depaul USA and management reserve the right to modify, add, or remove duties and assign other tasks as necessary.

jobs.description:
ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD.

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career.

The Role

AMD is seeking a Senior Program Manager, Data Center Strategy & Planning to build and scale the processes, governance, and tools that underpin AMD's data center strategy and acquisition function. Based in Santa Clara, CA and reporting to the CVP, Data Center Strategy & Acquisition, this leader will own program management across capacity planning, data center provider, AI Lab and NeoCloud partner diligence, regional expansion, and cross-functional operating standards for one of AMD's strategically important growth initiatives. 

In this highly visible role, you will partner closely with Corporate Development, GPUBU, Sales, Engineering, Legal, Government Affairs, and Security teams to ensure AMD's data center acquisition engine operates with the discipline, speed, and transparency the business requires. You will build the operating model for a fast-moving function, establish scalable processes and governance, evaluate data center capacity opportunities and partners, and provide executive visibility into capacity, capital, risk, and program status. 

This position offers the opportunity to help shape a function from the ground up, work directly with senior leaders across AMD and its data center developer, AI Lab, and NeoCloud partners, and apply modern AI tools, including ChatGPT and Claude, to automate and scale a program central to AMD's growth strategy. 

The Person

The ideal candidate is a builder who is energized by creating process and structure where none exists today and can move fluidly between hands-on program management and executive-level communication. You are equally comfortable managing a capacity plan tied to revenue goals, supporting due diligence on a data center provider's operational and financial maturity, and briefing executives on program status, often within the same week. 

You possess strong organizational and analytical skills, a bias toward action, and the judgment to determine when processes need to be formalized versus kept lightweight. You thrive in ambiguous, fast-growth environments, are comfortable driving change across stakeholders who do not report directly to you, and are genuinely curious about how AI tools can remove friction from recurring work. 

You are highly collaborative and able to build trusted relationships across Corporate Development, GPUBU business leadership, Sales, Engineering, Legal, Government Affairs, Security, and executive leadership. 

Key Responsibilities

Own data center capacity planning, ensuring capacity supports revenue goals and proactively managing changes to Ready-for-Service (RFS) timelines. 
Build and scale the Data Center Strategy & Acquisition operating model, including processes, governance, RACI, role clarity, and change management across the function.

Establish the New Region Expansion process and business justification framework to enable consistent prioritization and investment decisions. 
Drive development and adoption of cross-functional acquisition standards, including lease templates and processes spanning Legal, Government Affairs, physical security, logical security, and cybersecurity. 
Identify opportunities to automate recurring workflows, analysis, and reporting using ChatGPT, Claude, and other AI tools. 
Build and maintain executive dashboards and reporting that provide visibility into capacity, acquisition activity, key risks, dependencies, and overall program status. 

Preferred Experience

Experience in data center strategy, infrastructure strategy, technical program management, or a related infrastructure environment. 
Demonstrated success building and scaling new processes, operating models, governance frameworks, or cross-functional programs in a fast-growth or ambiguous environment. 
Experience evaluating data center providers, infrastructure partners, vendors, or strategic opportunities, including operational and financial due diligence.

Strong analytical and business skills, including proficiency with Excel, financial modeling, Power BI, PowerPoint, and executive-level data visualization and reporting.

ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS 

Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Finance, Real Estate, or a related field preferred.

jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Physical AI
jobs.description:
Apptronik is a human-centered robotics company developing AI-powered robots to support humanity in every facet of life. Our flagship humanoid robot, Apollo, is built to collaborate thoughtfully with people, starting with critical industries such as manufacturing and logistics, with future applications in healthcare, the home, and beyond.

We operate at the cutting edge of Applied AI, applying our expertise across the full robotics stack to solve some of society's most important problems. You will join a team dedicated to bringing Apollo to market at scale, tackling the complex challenges like safety, commercialization, and mass production to change the world for the better.

JOB SUMMARY

We are looking for a highly technical Staff or Principal Technical Program Manager to lead the programs that train Apollo's AI. This role owns the full physical AI training lifecycle: the compute infrastructure we train on, the data engine that feeds it, the pretraining, mid-training, and post-training runs that produce our models, and the path that takes those models onto robots in the field.

You will operate as a technical peer to research and infrastructure leadership, not a schedule keeper. You will set the strategy for how training programs are planned and resourced, own the build-out and utilization of our cloud and on-premises GPU capacity, and turn research goals into executable plans with clear gates and decisions. As the function grows, you will define the program management practices that let Apptronik train and ship models faster than anyone else in physical AI.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES or KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

Compute Strategy & Infrastructure:
Own the strategy and execution for Apptronik's training compute across cloud and on-premises GPUs. Drive capacity forecasting, build-vs-buy decisions, vendor and cloud partnerships, cluster bring-up, and the utilization, cost, and allocation of compute across research teams.
Training Program Execution:
Run pretraining, mid-training, fine-tuning, and distillation efforts as disciplined programs. Define compute budgets, data freeze dates, checkpoint and evaluation gates, and go/no-go criteria, and lead the response when a run diverges or infrastructure fails.
Data Engine:
Own the program that turns model needs into training data, spanning teleoperation, human demonstration, and simulation. Translate research requirements into collection plans, quality standards, and SOPs, and scale data throughput with the pipelines and storage behind it.
Evaluation & Model Release:
Establish a rigorous evaluation and release process across simulation and real robots. Drive statistically sound benchmarks, regression gates, and clear promotion criteria so release decisions rest on evidence, not demos.
Deployment & Fleet Learning:
Own the path from trained checkpoint to on-robot inference, including model optimization for edge hardware and integration with software, controls, and firmware. Build the loop that brings fleet data back into post-training and safely rolls out improved policies.
Ownership:
Own program execution end to end. Set strategic direction, identify resource requirements, and be accountable for delivering on company goals and roadmap. Challenge assumptions at the org level and foster a results-driven culture.
Communication:
Proactively communicate program status, risks, trade-offs, and decisions to executive stakeholders. Make compute, data, and model trade-offs legible to leadership and clearly articulate requirements, goals, and milestones across teams.
Leadership & Mentorship:
Mentor TPMs and engineers, and define the frameworks, tooling, and operating rhythms that let research move fast without losing rigor. Raise the technical bar of the program management function.

SKILLS AND REQUIREMENTS

Large-Scale Training Programs
— Deep experience leading programs for large model training, including pretraining, mid-training, fine-tuning, and distillation. Fluency in how runs are planned, resourced, monitored, and recovered when they fail.
GPU Compute & ML Infrastructure
— Hands-on understanding of GPU clusters across cloud and on-premises environments, including schedulers, distributed training, high-speed interconnects, and storage. Experience driving capacity planning, procurement, and cluster bring-up.
Hands-On Technical Depth
— Ability to read training code, interpret loss curves and evaluation results, and diagnose data and infrastructure issues alongside the team. Comfortable with Python and a modern framework such as PyTorch or JAX.
Robot Learning Data
— Experience with the data that drives physical AI: teleoperation, demonstration capture, simulation and synthetic data, annotation, and quality control at scale.
Evaluation Rigor
— Experience building evaluation frameworks and release criteria for ML models, ideally spanning simulation and real-world testing.
Edge Deployment
— Familiarity with taking models from training to on-device inference, including optimization for embedded and edge AI hardware.
Vendor & Partner Management
— Proven success managing cloud providers, hardware vendors, and data partners, including negotiating capacity and resolving cross-org dependencies.
Research Program Leadership
— Ability to plan around research uncertainty using experiments, decision points, and gates rather than fixed deliverables, while holding infrastructure and data work to firm commitments.
Influence in Resource-Constrained Environments
— Proven ability to allocate scarce compute and data across competing teams, align research, engineering, and executive leadership, and make hard prioritization calls.
Strategic Thinking
— Ability to translate company strategy into compute, data, and model roadmaps, and influence those roadmaps through data-driven insight.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or a related technical field required
10+ years of experience in technical program management, ML engineering, or ML infrastructure, including leading large-scale training or compute programs at a senior, staff, or principal level
Preferred: Experience at a frontier AI lab, hyperscaler, or robotics foundation model company
Preferred: Experience standing up or scaling GPU clusters or data center capacity
Preferred: Direct experience with robot learning, vision-language-action models, or large-scale robot data programs
Preferred: Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times
Vision to read printed materials and a computer screen
Hearing and speech to communicate

The salary range for this position is $240,000 - $280,000

This is a direct hire. Please, no outside Agency solicitations.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Brand Studio lays the foundations that help Stripe accelerate. We do this by creating, evolving, and maintaining Stripe’s high-quality, versatile, and forward-looking brand design systems, experiences, and advertising campaigns. We sweat the details. We make it seem effortless.

What you’ll do

You will be responsible for leading brand design operations and creative production across all of Stripe’s internal and external events, in close partnership with the Experiential Creative Director. This role is a hybrid mix of program management, project management, and creative production depending on the project phase. During certain periods you’ll be focused on the 10,000 foot view of the program, and at other times you’ll be working side-by-side with the Design team overseeing execution of every design detail before an event.

Responsibilities

Manage a high volume of simultaneous projects, ranging from small to large scale

Navigate challenges and blockers with ease; proactive in finding solutions, and always looking ahead for the team
Uphold and advocate for design quality with cross-functional teams and vendors to exceed engagement and registration goals
Inspire and sustain a culture of excellence by collaborating with creatives in best practices and processes

Who you are

Staff Program Managers within Brand Studio at Stripe demonstrate passion for great design and have strong design sense. They’re experts in diving deep into details, expanding, evolving, defining, and documenting flexible systems and processes that achieve bar-raising quality and consistency at scale.

The ideal candidate excels at keeping the work on track while maintaining (and raising) the bar on craft. They offer options and tradeoffs, crisply articulate decisions, iterate quickly, and collaborate seamlessly with senior leadership, marketers, creatives, and agency partners. Most importantly, they are meticulous when it comes to details.

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Requirements

10+ years of experience in similar roles and industries
Think users first—understand their needs, find interesting and unique solutions, and strive to consistently optimize how to best engage with them
Have a strong strategic acumen for developing complex program roadmaps and cross-functional processes in a fast-paced environment
Can demonstrate strong design sense, industry knowledge and best practices, have deep knowledge producing complex brand and event design systems, and bringing design assets to life across the creative production process
Proven excellence in producing creative systems that are optimized for scale and growth
Highly detail oriented and excel at simplifying complexity
Strong track record successfully influencing outcomes both internally and with agency partners
Can balance optimizing for speed and quality, with high craft and quality creative work
Are persuasive in explaining your work, process, and decisions
Excellent organization and presentation skills, and excel in written and verbal communication
Are passionate about Stripe’s mission

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Stripes on the Works in Progress team based in the London, UK office also work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $184,000 - $276,000. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

You will lead complex, cross-functional programs, turning emerging AI capabilities into secure, reliable, and reusable solutions. Working closely with engineering leaders and teams across the organization, you will drive platform delivery, establish operating models, and coordinate adoption across multiple business areas. You will also shape AI readiness by identifying gaps in skills, tooling, integrations, and governance, then building practical programs to address them. This is a high-impact opportunity to establish the foundations of a new Agentic Engineering function in a remote, fast-moving technology environment. The role combines strategic program leadership, technical fluency, organizational change, and hands-on experimentation with AI-enabled workflows.

Accountabilities

Partner with the Agentic Engineering team to define and manage the platform roadmap, milestones, dependencies, and delivery plans across reusable agents, workflow orchestration, context and knowledge access, tool integrations, evaluation, observability, and governance.
Coordinate the development and integration of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and other tools that engineering teams need to work effectively.
Establish and manage the team's operating cadence, including planning sessions, delivery reviews, decision logs, risk tracking, exception management, and retrospectives.
Make trade-offs involving scope, capacity, cost, model usage, compute resources, and delivery risks visible to stakeholders early.
Build an intake and prioritization framework for AI use cases and platform needs across Retail, Hospitality, Payments, and platform teams.
Coordinate early-adopter launches, gather feedback, and turn successful use cases into reusable patterns that can be adopted by other teams.
Partner with Engineering to define evaluation standards for agent quality, reliability, security, cost, and human oversight before AI solutions enter production workflows.
Coordinate Security, Privacy, Legal, Data, and Architecture stakeholders to integrate governance reviews and approvals into the delivery lifecycle.
Drive AI readiness across Product, Engineering, and Design by assessing individual capabilities, skills, and working practices, as well as organizational tooling, licenses, configurations, integrations, access, and permissions.
Work with Product and Technology leaders to move teams beyond basic AI tool usage toward measurable improvements in workflows, productivity, and customer value.
Collaborate with the Product Development Lifecycle (PDLC) Technical Program Manager to align platform adoption with shared processes, baseline metrics, and performance objectives.
Partner with the Learning and Development Technical Program Manager to build and deliver enablement initiatives, including workshops, champion networks, and train-the-trainer programs.
Report program progress, delivery health, risks, readiness gaps, adoption signals, and key trade-offs to senior leadership.
Use AI agents and automation to improve program management activities such as status reporting, risk detection, follow-ups, and decision tracking, demonstrating measurable results.

Requirements

At least 8 years of technical program management experience at the platform, infrastructure, or developer-experience level, with ownership of complex, multi-team programs.
Hands-on familiarity with AI development tools and infrastructure, including coding assistants, MCP-based integrations, configuration, and access management.
Practical understanding of AI-enabled and agentic systems, including orchestration, tool use, retrieval and context management, evaluations, observability, and human-in-the-loop controls.
Experience delivering internal platforms or shared engineering capabilities to multiple teams or internal customers with different priorities.
Proven ability to establish and standardize engineering practices across organizations while allowing for differences in team needs and workflows.
Experience building a program or operating model from the ground up, including governance, intake processes, delivery cadence, and stakeholder mechanisms.
Track record of partnering with Security, Privacy, Legal, or Risk teams to deliver technology programs in regulated or sensitive environments.
Strong technical judgment and the ability to challenge engineering decisions constructively, particularly around AI platform capabilities and operational readiness.
Excellent executive communication skills, with the ability to present program progress, risks, dependencies, and trade-offs clearly to senior leaders.
Demonstrated ability to influence and align senior stakeholders without relying on formal authority.
Experience using AI and automation to improve and scale program management practices, supported by practical examples of tools or workflows implemented.
Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to navigate ambiguity and manage complex dependencies.

The Senior Program Manager will build and lead Forj Medical's manufacturing transfer program from the ground up. Sitting within Operations, this role owns the planning and execution of production line transfers, site transfers, and site decommissioning activities, including transfers to our Costa Rica facility and other locations outside the United States.This is a foundational role. You will set how transfer programs are planned, tracked, and executed at Forj Medical, and as the transfer portfolio grows, you will have the opportunity to scale the function and help hire the team.

Build the transfer program function from the ground up, establishing the standard approach, tools, templates, and governance for production line and site transfers.
Lead multiple concurrent transfer programs end to end, including transfer strategy, stakeholder alignment, knowledge transfer, documentation readiness, equipment and process transition, validation support, training, production ramp, and post-transfer stabilization.
Build realistic, defensible schedules grounded in a working knowledge of equipment, processes, and operator and assembler learning curves. Independently assess and challenge estimates from sending and receiving sites, including during site closures, where input may be incomplete or overly optimistic.
Develop and own detailed program plans in MS Project/Planner or comparable project management software, including schedules, resource allocation, budgets, and milestones.
Direct program execution with minimal oversight, including schedule adherence, budget, scope changes, risk and issue management, and escalation of anything impacting schedule, quality, cost, or regulatory expectations.
Lead cross-site and international transfer activities, with significant coordination with the Costa Rica site, ensuring clear communication across time zones and clear ownership of roles and responsibilities.
Lead cross-functional teams in a matrixed environment, balancing urgency and accountability with empathy for employees affected by site transitions and closures.
Report program status, risks, and recommendations to Operations leadership.
Partner with the customer-facing Program Management Office to keep customer commitments aligned with transfer plans.
Continuously improve Forj Medical's transfer processes and define the future-state structure of the transfer program function.

B.S. or M.S. required, preferably in a technical, engineering, operations, or related field; PMP certification a plus.
8+ years of project or program management experience in medical device manufacturing (OEM or contract manufacturing).

Strong technical and operational understanding of manufacturing equipment, processes, and training needs, sufficient to validate timelines and resource requirements.

Experience building or scaling a program management function, process, or team preferred.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to convey technical and business concepts clearly to leadership, engineers, and production teams.

new_jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Change & Transformation
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?

RBC's AI-Driven Software Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) program is scaling across Technology & Operations through a franchise model. A central team owns the method, platform, measurement and playbook. Each L3 (Senior Executive) acts as a franchise, owning local execution, adoption and sustained ownership under a named AI-DLC Lead. With a target of 15,000 staff enabled by mid-FY27, the model depends on clear process and disciplined program management.

As Senior Program Manager, Change & Transformation, you will own delivery of the Franchise Model rollout, reporting to the Delivery & Exec Lead, Live Programs. You will be accountable for moving each L3 from kickoff to steady state on time: entry gates passed, 12-week adoption plan on track, and Central teams delivering what each L3 needs.

You will plan and sequence the rollout, coordinate L3 Leads and Central teams (Change & Learning, Platform, Benefits & Baseline), run the gate and waiver process with Technology ESG, and give decision-makers accurate, timely information. You must be comfortable in a high-visibility environment and able to hold direct conversations with Senior Director-level AI-DLC Leads about unmet gates.

WHAT WILL YOU DO?

Rollout Planning: Own the end-to-end L3 franchise rollout plan: sequencing, milestones, dependencies and calendar, from kickoff through steady state.
Entry Gates & Waivers: Drive each L3 through the five entry gates (roles staffed, readiness assessed, plan signed, platform ready, champion layer active) with L3 Leads and Technology ESG. Run the waiver process with a gap, closing date and owner, surface expiring waivers early, and allow no silent renewals.
Adoption & Readiness: Support each L3 through the 12-week adoption plan and readiness assessment, including white-glove or self-serve triage. Flag drift against handbook milestones and agree corrective actions with the Lead.

Tātaki Auckland Unlimited (TAU) is Auckland’s cultural, events and destination agency. It enriches the cultural life and vibrancy of Auckland through events, experiences and taonga (treasures). Its work connects communities, celebrates identity, and grows Auckland’s reputation as a world-class place to live, visit and belong. TAU is a proud Auckland Council-controlled organisation.

He angitūtanga: The opportunity

Auckland Zoo has an exciting full-time opportunity for an Operational Health, Safety & Security Manager to help ensure the Zoo remains a safe, secure, and resilient environment for our people, animals, visitors, and partners. Reporting to the Head of Zoo Environment, Design and Construction, you will provide specialist operational advice across health and safety, physical security, and emergency preparedness. Working alongside operational leaders, animal care teams, visitor experience, facilities, contractors, and external agencies, you will develop practical systems and controls that are clearly understood and consistently applied across daily operations, animal activities, construction projects, special events, and emergency situations.

In this role, and in collaboration with TAU partners and stakeholders you will:

Lead workplace inspections, assurance reviews, and incident investigations, using performance trends and lessons learned to strengthen safety and security practices.
Develop and maintain operational procedures, safe systems of work, the Zoo Emergency Management Plan and Procedures and Business Continuity Plan, and supporting documentation in line with legislation and organisational standards.
Review operational risk assessments, contractor plans, and high-risk activities, providing practical advice on critical controls across projects, animal operations, visitor experiences, and events.
Coordinate physical and operational security, including CCTV, access control, alarms, restricted keys, perimeter protection, and contracted security services, while maintaining relationships with Police and emergency services.
Strengthen emergency preparedness and organisational capability by coordinating exercises, training, inductions and briefings, and coaching leaders and teams in risk management and safe working practices.

Click this link for the full position description

He kōrero mōu: About you

You will be a confident and solutions-focused health, safety and security professional who can turn a clear vision into practical action. Comfortable navigating complexity and ambiguity, you will assess risk, make sound decisions and step forward constructively when difficult issues need to be addressed. You will build trusted partnerships across operational teams, contractors and external agencies while holding yourself and others accountable for agreed standards and commitments. An engaging communicator and coach, you will bring people together around shared objectives, value diverse perspectives and help create a proactive, learning-focused, and risk-aware culture.

To be successful in this role, you will have:

At least five years’ experience in operational health, safety and security, or a closely related role, supported by a formal health and safety qualification or equivalent professional experience.
Strong knowledge of operational risk management, legislation, standards, and industry guidance, with experience reviewing safety plans, risk assessments, and contractor documentation.
Demonstrated experience developing operational procedures and safe systems of work, as well as conducting inspections, audits, or other assurance activities.
Effective communication, facilitation and coaching skills, the ability to manage competing priorities within a dynamic operational environment, and a current full New Zealand driver licence.

This is a unique career opportunity working within the lush, green environment of Auckland Zoo, where we welcome more than 850 thousand visitors annually. new_jobs.title: Data Analyst (Information Management Associate)
new_jobs.description:
As SISSIRP advances into full implementation, there is a critical need for structured information management to ensure that field data is systematically collected, cleaned, analyzed, and translated into actionable programme intelligence for project management, donor reporting, and decision-making. The programme currently operates across multiple data streams — physical progress, WASH outputs, quality assessments, procurement milestones, and beneficiary data — that require integration, visualization, and quality control to meet AfDB M&E and reporting standards.
Under the direct supervision of the Programme Officer (Engineering) and the overall guidance of the Programme Manager, the Information Management Associate will serve as the dedicated IM focal point for the SISSIRP programme. The incumbent will design, maintain, and continuously improve the programme’s data collection systems, analytical products, and reporting dashboards, enabling senior programme staff and client management to make evidence-based decisions throughout the project lifecycle.

Responsibilities and Accountabilities

1. Data Collection Systems – KoBoToolbox

Design, build, and maintain KoBoToolbox data collection forms for all programme components, including physical progress monitoring, QA/QC inspections, WASH output tracking, beneficiary data, and field verification exercises; ensure forms are version-controlled, piloted, and deployed consistently across all four project states.
Manage the end-to-end data pipeline from field submission through KoBoToolbox to consolidated datasets: monitor submission rates, identify and resolve data gaps, run automated validation checks (range, logic, required fields), and flag anomalies to field engineers for correction.
Develop and maintain standardized data collection protocols and field data submission procedures; conduct remote and in-person training sessions for site engineers and state-level staff on KoBoToolbox form usage, data quality standards, and submission workflows.
Support integration of KoBoToolbox data exports with downstream analysis and reporting tools (Excel, Power BI), ensuring data formats, coding conventions, and field labels are consistent and transformation-ready.
Maintain and document all active KoBoToolbox projects, form versions, user permissions, and data export schedules; ensure data is backed up and stored in line with IOM data governance standards.

2. Data Analysis and Visualization – Excel & Power BI

Build and maintain Advanced Excel workbooks for programme data management and analysis, including:

- Dynamic pivot tables linked to live data exports.
- Data reconciliation across multiple registers.
- Structured data validation and dropdown controls to enforce data integrity.
- Conditional formatting for status flags, overdue items, and threshold breaches.
- Automated summary dashboards using Excel formulas and slicers to generate programme KPIs without manual recalculation.
Develop, publish, and maintain Power BI dashboards providing real-time programme intelligence for SISSIRP management and AfDB reporting. Dashboards should cover:

- Physical progress by state, sector, and facility type.
- Procurement and contract milestone tracking.
- WASH output indicators (coverage, functionality, beneficiary reach).
- QA/QC pass/fail rates.
- Financial disbursement progress against targets.
Apply DAX measures and calculated columns in Power BI to derive programme-level KPIs (e.g., % facilities completed, cost per beneficiary, average construction duration) and configure row-level security to control data access by state and role.
Design and implement data models in Power BI connecting multiple source tables (progress trackers, procurement registers, beneficiary data, KoBoToolbox exports) via defined relationships, ensuring dashboard figures reconcile with source data.
Produce periodic analytical reports and data summaries (weekly, monthly, quarterly) for the Programme Officer, Programme Manager, and donor reporting requirements; translate data outputs into clear narrative findings with supporting charts and maps.
Support GIS-based analysis and mapping of SISSIRP facilities using available tools (Excel/Power BI map visuals, QGIS where applicable) to visualize geographic distribution of project activities and outputs.

3. Programme Reporting and M&E Support

Serve as the IM focal point for all AfDB progress reporting requirements: compile, quality-check, and format data inputs from field teams into the programme’s standard reporting templates in line with AfDB M&E frameworks and SISSIRP’s Results Framework indicators.
Maintain the SISSIRP master data register: a single source of truth for all facility-level progress data, updated on a rolling basis from field inputs, reconciled against procurement and payment records, and shared with the Programme Officer and Programme Manager on a weekly basis.
Support the preparation of donor progress reports, quarterly reviews, and AfDB supervision mission briefings by providing accurate, well-visualized data summaries, programme maps, and indicator tables.
Maintain the programme’s document management system for IM-related files, including data dictionaries, codebooks, form versions, and dashboard user guides.

4. IM Capacity Support and Quality Assurance

Provide ongoing technical support and troubleshooting to field teams on KoBoToolbox, Excel, and Power BI; respond to data queries from site engineers and state-level staff within one working day.
Develop and maintain user guides, data dictionaries, and standard operating procedures for all IM tools and systems used under SISSIRP.
Conduct periodic data quality reviews across all programme components; produce data quality assessment reports with findings and corrective recommendations for the Programme Officer.
Perform such other duties as may be assigned by the Programme Officer (Engineering) or Programme Manager.

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education & Experience – Minimum Requirements

Bachelor’s Degree in Information Management, Statistics, Data Science, Computer Science, or a related field from an accredited academic institution, with four years of relevant professional experience; or
Completed High School Degree / Certificate with six years of relevant professional experience.
Demonstrated hands-on experience with KoBoToolbox (or ODK/Kobo Collect): designing multi-section forms with skip logic, validation constraints, and repeat groups; managing projects and user permissions; exporting and cleaning datasets.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including:

- Dynamic pivot tables and pivot charts.
- VLOOKUP, INDEX-MATCH, XLOOKUP.
- Nested IF / IFS, COUNTIFS, SUMIFS.
- Data validation and structured tables.
- Power Query for data transformation.
- Conditional formatting and dashboard construction.
Demonstrated experience building and publishing Power BI reports and dashboards, including data model design, DAX measures, calculated columns, and Power BI Service publishing and access management.
Familiarity with infrastructure, WASH, or humanitarian programme data is a strong advantage.
Experience with QGIS or other GIS tools for mapping and spatial analysis is an advantage.

Skills

Expert-level proficiency in KoBoToolbox: form design (XLSForm or online builder), skip logic, validation constraints, repeat groups, multi-language forms, data export, and project management.
Advanced Excel: pivot tables, VLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH/XLOOKUP, Power Query (M language), nested formulas, data validation, conditional formatting, dynamic dashboards without VBA.
Power BI: data modelling (star schema), DAX (CALCULATE, FILTER, RELATED, time-intelligence), report design principles, Power BI Service (workspaces, row-level security, scheduled refresh, sharing).
Strong analytical and data quality skills: ability to identify and resolve inconsistencies, outliers, and gaps in field datasets.
Clear data communication skills: ability to translate raw datasets into concise visual summaries, charts, and written findings for non-technical audiences.
Proficiency in Microsoft SharePoint / OneDrive for IM file management and team data sharing.
Working knowledge of Results Frameworks, Indicator Tracking Tables, and logframe-based M&E; familiarity with AfDB reporting standards is a strong advantage.
Ability to manage multiple analytical workstreams simultaneously and deliver outputs to tight deadlines.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy, consistency, and audit-readiness.

DELIVERABLES
The Information Management Associate shall produce and maintain the following on an ongoing basis:
Maintained and operational KoBoToolbox data collection system across all SISSIRP programme components and states, with version-controlled forms, active user management, and documented protocols.
Weekly SISSIRP Master Data Register update: facility-level progress, procurement, and WASH output data consolidated, cleaned, and shared with the Programme Officer.
Power BI dashboard suite (programme overview, state-level progress, WASH outputs, procurement milestones) — published, refreshed, and shared with programme management on a rolling basis.
Monthly data quality assessment report: submission rates, error flags, correction actions, and unresolved gaps.
Quarterly IM inputs for AfDB progress reporting: data tables, indicator summaries, maps, and charts formatted to AfDB reporting standards.
IM system documentation: data dictionary, KoBoToolbox form register, Power BI user guide, and standard operating procedures — kept current and accessible to the programme team.

Mission

Depaul USA supports homeless and marginalized people, providing people experiencing homelessness with purpose and hope for a positive future. Our vision is that everyone has a place to call home and a stake in his or her community. In cities across the nation, we meet people where they are to address their needs. Through a combination of homelessness services and a growing social enterprise portfolio, Depaul USA is innovating and bringing real solutions to those facing homelessness.

Depaul USA Is a Growing, National, Not-for-profit Organization That Serves More Than 7,000 People Annually And Has a Combined Operating And Capital Budget In Excess Of $12.5 Million. Our Vincentian Values Underpin What We Do

We celebrate the potential of people;
We put our words into action;
We aim to take a wider role in civil society; and
We believe in rights and responsibilities.

Please visit www.depaulusa.org to learn more.

Depaul USA is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace, and we are firmly committed to creating an equitable and inclusive environment for all employees. If you need a reasonable accommodation in any part of the hiring process, please let us know.

Position Description

The Program Manager (PM) is responsible for the overall management and daily operations of Casa Milagrosa, a day resource center serving individuals experiencing homelessness or housing instability. The PM oversees all center staff, volunteers, facility operations, and program services to ensure a safe, welcoming, and effective environment for participants. The PM reports to the Los Angeles City Director, who provides overall oversight of Casa Milagrosa.

Primary Duties And Responsibilities

Essential Job Functions

Oversees the overall daily operations of Casa Milagrosa, ensuring the center operates effectively and meets the needs of participants.
Manages daily opening and closing procedures, staffing coverage, and coordination of program activities.
Maintains a safe, clean, organized, and welcoming environment for participants, staff, volunteers, and visitors.
Oversees facility needs, maintenance coordination, and the ordering, purchasing, and inventory of food, beverages, snacks, cleaning products, program supplies, and other materials necessary for daily operations.
Ensures program procedures, safety expectations, and organizational policies are consistently followed.
Responds to emergencies, participant concerns, conflicts, and other urgent situations.
Directly supervises all staff assigned to Casa Milagrosa and coordinates volunteer activities.
Provides regular individual supervision, guidance, training, and feedback to support staff performance and professional development.
Coordinates staff schedules, responsibilities, and daily activities to ensure appropriate coverage and effective service delivery.
Addresses staff performance and accountability concerns and communicates significant staffing or operational issues to the Los Angeles City Director.
Ensures participants are treated with dignity and respect and receive appropriate support in a safe and welcoming environment.
Works closely with the Case Manager to ensure participant needs are addressed and appropriate services and resources are available.
Provides direct assistance to participants as needed, including helping them access housing, employment opportunities, community resources, and other supportive services.
Assists with participant intake, enrollment, and referrals while the Case Manager maintains primary responsibility for assigned client caseloads and case management services.
Addresses participant concerns and difficult situations in a sensitive, professional, and appropriate manner.
Maintains program records and tracks participant enrollment, attendance, activities, outputs, and outcomes.
Ensures required program documentation, reports, and statistics are completed accurately and submitted within established timelines.
Monitors program activities and identifies opportunities to improve service delivery and overall program effectiveness.
Works with the Los Angeles City Director to review program needs, performance, and operational priorities.

Additional Tasks and Responsibilities

Builds and maintains positive working relationships with community organizations, housing providers, service agencies, and other community stakeholders.
Participates in community coalition meetings and other collaborative activities that support the program's mission.
Assists with facility tours and provides information about Casa Milagrosa to visitors, volunteers, community partners, and other stakeholders.
Collaborates with the Case Manager, Los Angeles City Director, and other organizational staff to support program goals and organizational priorities.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

General Responsibilities

Stays informed of current local and national events, trends, and issues that impact Depaul USA’s work with people experiencing homelessness.
Strives continuously to develop the role in collaboration with the supervisor to ensure that all tasks are undertaken effectively and appropriately, meeting the strategic goals and objectives of Depaul USA.
Participates in internal and external meetings as required, attends training events, conferences, and other functions as necessary.
Participates in regular supervision and annual evaluations, identifying personal developmental and training needs.
Ensures adherence to all Depaul USA policies and procedures, particularly those relating to Health and Safety, Safeguarding, and the Code of Practice and Confidentiality.
Contributes to the effective implementation of Depaul USA’s Equal Opportunities Policy as it affects both the organization and its work with this participant group.
Undertakes the role in a professional manner, maintaining a highquality standard of work in accordance with the Vision, Mission, and Values of Depaul USA.
Undertakes any other duties that may be required which are commensurate with the role.

Qualifications

Qualifications

The ideal Program Manager will have experience managing programs and working with individuals experiencing homelessness or housing instability, including those facing mental health challenges, cognitive disabilities, and substance use disorders. The candidate should have an understanding of community resources and social service systems, along with the leadership and organizational skills necessary to oversee daily program operations and supervise staff. The successful candidate will possess the following qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Social Work or a closely related field, with at least two years of experience working with individuals experiencing homelessness and/or behavioral health challenges.
Experience supervising staff, coordinating program activities, or managing daily operations in a social services or nonprofit setting preferred.
Strong communication, interpersonal, problemsolving, and conflict resolution skills.
Ability to organize and prioritize multiple responsibilities, coordinate people and activities, and delegate effectively.
Sound judgment, decisionmaking skills, and the ability to work independently while knowing when to seek guidance.
Strong computer skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
Spanish fluency strongly preferred.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions. In the course of performing the job, the person in this position typically spends time sitting, standing, climbing stairs, walking, driving, carrying (20lbs), lifting (20lbs), operating a computer keyboard, and making and receiving telephone calls. Subjected to outside environmental conditions.

Work Schedule:

Primarily inperson at Casa Milagrosa in Los Angeles, CA.
Regular schedule is Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. 3:30 p.m. Pacific Time.
Must be available to support special events and program activities that may take place during evenings and weekends.

Benefits:

Medical, dental, and vision coverage options for the employee and eligible dependents.

401(k) Retirement plan with employer match.
Generous Vacation, Sick, and Personal leave and 10 Observed holidays.

AMD is seeking a Senior Program Manager, Data Center Strategy & Planning to build and scale the processes, governance, and tools that underpin AMD's data center strategy and acquisition function. In this highly visible role, you will partner closely with Corporate Development, GPUBU, Sales, Engineering, Legal, Government Affairs, and Security teams to ensure AMD's data center acquisition engine operates with the discipline, speed, and transparency the business requires. new_jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Physical AI
new_jobs.description:
Apptronik is a human-centered robotics company developing AI-powered robots to support humanity in every facet of life. Our flagship humanoid robot, Apollo, is built to collaborate thoughtfully with people, starting with critical industries such as manufacturing and logistics, with future applications in healthcare, the home, and beyond.

We operate at the cutting edge of Applied AI, applying our expertise across the full robotics stack to solve some of society's most important problems. You will join a team dedicated to bringing Apollo to market at scale, tackling the complex challenges like safety, commercialization, and mass production to change the world for the better.

JOB SUMMARY

We are looking for a highly technical Staff or Principal Technical Program Manager to lead the programs that train Apollo's AI. This role owns the full physical AI training lifecycle: the compute infrastructure we train on, the data engine that feeds it, the pretraining, mid-training, and post-training runs that produce our models, and the path that takes those models onto robots in the field.

You will operate as a technical peer to research and infrastructure leadership, not a schedule keeper. You will set the strategy for how training programs are planned and resourced, own the build-out and utilization of our cloud and on-premises GPU capacity, and turn research goals into executable plans with clear gates and decisions. As the function grows, you will define the program management practices that let Apptronik train and ship models faster than anyone else in physical AI.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES or KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

Compute Strategy & Infrastructure:
Own the strategy and execution for Apptronik's training compute across cloud and on-premises GPUs. Drive capacity forecasting, build-vs-buy decisions, vendor and cloud partnerships, cluster bring-up, and the utilization, cost, and allocation of compute across research teams.
Training Program Execution:
Run pretraining, mid-training, fine-tuning, and distillation efforts as disciplined programs. Define compute budgets, data freeze dates, checkpoint and evaluation gates, and go/no-go criteria, and lead the response when a run diverges or infrastructure fails.
Data Engine:
Own the program that turns model needs into training data, spanning teleoperation, human demonstration, and simulation. Translate research requirements into collection plans, quality standards, and SOPs, and scale data throughput with the pipelines and storage behind it.
Evaluation & Model Release:
Establish a rigorous evaluation and release process across simulation and real robots. Drive statistically sound benchmarks, regression gates, and clear promotion criteria so release decisions rest on evidence, not demos.
Deployment & Fleet Learning:
Own the path from trained checkpoint to on-robot inference, including model optimization for edge hardware and integration with software, controls, and firmware. Build the loop that brings fleet data back into post-training and safely rolls out improved policies.
Ownership:
Own program execution end to end. Set strategic direction, identify resource requirements, and be accountable for delivering on company goals and roadmap. Challenge assumptions at the org level and foster a results-driven culture.
Communication:
Proactively communicate program status, risks, trade-offs, and decisions to executive stakeholders. Make compute, data, and model trade-offs legible to leadership and clearly articulate requirements, goals, and milestones across teams.
Leadership & Mentorship:
Mentor TPMs and engineers, and define the frameworks, tooling, and operating rhythms that let research move fast without losing rigor. Raise the technical bar of the program management function.

SKILLS AND REQUIREMENTS

Large-Scale Training Programs
— Deep experience leading programs for large model training, including pretraining, mid-training, fine-tuning, and distillation. Fluency in how runs are planned, resourced, monitored, and recovered when they fail.
GPU Compute & ML Infrastructure
— Hands-on understanding of GPU clusters across cloud and on-premises environments, including schedulers, distributed training, high-speed interconnects, and storage. Experience driving capacity planning, procurement, and cluster bring-up.
Hands-On Technical Depth
— Ability to read training code, interpret loss curves and evaluation results, and diagnose data and infrastructure issues alongside the team. Comfortable with Python and a modern framework such as PyTorch or JAX.
Robot Learning Data
— Experience with the data that drives physical AI: teleoperation, demonstration capture, simulation and synthetic data, annotation, and quality control at scale.
Evaluation Rigor
— Experience building evaluation frameworks and release criteria for ML models, ideally spanning simulation and real-world testing.
Edge Deployment
— Familiarity with taking models from training to on-device inference, including optimization for embedded and edge AI hardware.
Vendor & Partner Management
— Proven success managing cloud providers, hardware vendors, and data partners, including negotiating capacity and resolving cross-org dependencies.
Research Program Leadership
— Ability to plan around research uncertainty using experiments, decision points, and gates rather than fixed deliverables, while holding infrastructure and data work to firm commitments.
Influence in Resource-Constrained Environments
— Proven ability to allocate scarce compute and data across competing teams, align research, engineering, and executive leadership, and make hard prioritization calls.
Strategic Thinking
— Ability to translate company strategy into compute, data, and model roadmaps, and influence those roadmaps through data-driven insight.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or a related technical field required
10+ years of experience in technical program management, ML engineering, or ML infrastructure, including leading large-scale training or compute programs at a senior, staff, or principal level
Preferred: Experience at a frontier AI lab, hyperscaler, or robotics foundation model company
Preferred: Experience standing up or scaling GPU clusters or data center capacity
Preferred: Direct experience with robot learning, vision-language-action models, or large-scale robot data programs
Preferred: Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times
Vision to read printed materials and a computer screen
Hearing and speech to communicate

Partner closely with the Experiential Creative Director to further scale and evolve event design at Stripe; optimize processes to streamline how work is done
Partner closely with the Corporate Events team to ensure smooth execution and integration of event brand design across all surfaces
Ensure smooth collaboration with leadership, creatives, cross-functional partners, and vendors

Navigate challenges and blockers with ease; proactive in finding solutions, and always looking ahead for the team

Inspire and sustain a culture of excellence by collaborating with creatives in best practices and processes

Who you are

Staff Program Managers within Brand Studio at Stripe demonstrate passion for great design and have strong design sense. They’re experts in diving deep into details, expanding, evolving, defining, and documenting flexible systems and processes that achieve bar-raising quality and consistency at scale.

The ideal candidate excels at keeping the work on track while maintaining (and raising) the bar on craft. They offer options and tradeoffs, crisply articulate decisions, iterate quickly, and collaborate seamlessly with senior leadership, marketers, creatives, and agency partners. 10+ years of experience in similar roles and industries
Think users first—understand their needs, find interesting and unique solutions, and strive to consistently optimize how to best engage with them
Have a strong strategic acumen for developing complex program roadmaps and cross-functional processes in a fast-paced environment

Proven excellence in producing creative systems that are optimized for scale and growth
Highly detail oriented and excel at simplifying complexity
Strong track record successfully influencing outcomes both internally and with agency partners
Can balance optimizing for speed and quality, with high craft and quality creative work
Are persuasive in explaining your work, process, and decisions
Excellent organization and presentation skills, and excel in written and verbal communication
Are passionate about Stripe’s mission

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $184,000 - $276,000. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.
